name: interner-strong-spike

variantDescriptions.weak: #84 tip `f06dc23f02` + the interner switches (`6c7200e37c`), switches off: today's weak interners
variantDescriptions.strong: the same build, `-Ddotty.uniques.strong=true`: entries hold their types strongly, no weak references
variantDescriptions.uncache: the same build, `-Ddotty.uniques.uncacheMethodParams=true`: types over method/poly params not hash-consed (retronym/scala3#21)
variantDescriptions.weak2: A/A twin of `weak` (a marker property only)
variantDescriptions.strong2: A/A twin of `strong` (a marker property only)

description: The type interners as a benchmarking fixture and an architecture question: weak (today) against strong, run-scoped entries (as in rustc, clang and Swift), and against not hash-consing ephemeral types over method and poly params (retronym/scala3#21, −11% on scalaz against main). One build, the variants differ only in JVM flags. With A/A twins of `weak` and `strong`: does the strong interner reduce fork-to-fork variance?
dotc and scalaz to `-Ystop-after:typer`, ordinary GC (the weak references' GC cost is part of the question), xctrace `loads`, patched JDK 26, 3 rounds.
